newsitem.title: ISRAEL: RESEARCH ALERT-Claridge's Koor stake said positive.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT-Claridge's Koor stake said positive.

text.p: Lehman Brothers said Claridge Israel's purchase of a 10.2 percent stake in Koor Industries was a positive development.

Claridge last week paid $187 million for half of Shamrock's 20.4 percent stake with a 90-day option to buy the remaining half for the same price. Claridge acquired another 1.6 percent off the floor for $30 million.

"We view the Claridge-Shamrock deal as a positive move for the company. First, it ends a standing disagreement between Koor's CEO, Benny Gaon, and Shamrock's president Stanley Gold over the company's future," analyst Elise Horowitz said in a report.
"Second, we see the Claridge group bringing a new perspective to Koor along with facilitating and expediting some delayed strategic decisions."
Once the Claridge deal is finalised in 90 days Koor management will consider different options to increase shareholder value, Horowitz said.

"Possibilities in the near future include the sale or offering of private subsidiary Mashav, the 20 percent sale of cement monopoly Nesher to a global strategic partner, the restructuring of its agrochemical activities, including a U.S. offering and a public offering of telecom equipment manufacturer Telrad, of which Nortel owns a 20 percent stake."

Lehman expects Koor to report weak second-quarter earnings, 192 million shekels versus 209 million a year earlier, due to a slowdown in the Israeli economy and lower telecom sales. But it sees upside to the share price due to stronger results expected in the third and fourth quarters.
Koor shares are trading at an 18 percent discount to Lehman's net asset valuation and a 1997 multiple of 9.5 times estimated earnings.
"We continue to view this stock as an attractive investment opportunity and reiterate our 2-Outperform rating."
